edges.effect_quant: In a meta-analysis of maternal biomarkers, folate was lower in NTD-affected pregnancies (RoM 0.93, 95% CI 0.88 to 0.97), and classic randomized trials found 0 NTDs among 2471 multivitamin-exposed pregnancies versus 6 among 2391 controls in one study.
edges.population: women of reproductive age and periconceptional pregnancies
edges.mechanism: Folate is central to one-carbon metabolism, nucleotide synthesis, and methylation during early embryogenesis. Inadequate folate around conception can impair neural tube closure during the narrow developmental window when the defect arises.
edges.summary: The evidence linking low folate status to neural tube defects is unusually strong and consistent across biomarker meta-analysis and classic randomized prevention trials. This is one of the clearer nutrition-to-outcome relationships in the literature, with the main uncertainty being dose strategy rather than direction.
edges.caveats: Most intervention evidence concerns periconceptional supplementation rather than later pregnancy correction, and multivitamin trials do not isolate folate perfectly from co-administered nutrients. Even so, the direction and public-health relevance are exceptionally well established.
